summary: A 1921 Aermotor-built tower listed at 47 ft in Elk State Forest, Cameron County; one storymap entry is the only source for its history.

facts.design: Built by the Aermotor Windmill Company, per the storymap; no design details given
facts.status_note: Only the storymap describes this tower, in the present tense; no later inspection or second source was found.

events.note: Storymap: built by Aermotor Windmill Company, 47 ft. Single source for this date.
Lumber era in the area of Elk State Forest ended

evidence.quote: Located in Cameron County in Elk State Forest.
Built in 1921 by the Aermotor Windmill Company.
It has a height of 47 feet.

evidence.supports: Aermotor made galvanized steel fire lookouts under the name Aermotor Corporation
evidence.quote: The company also manufactured galvanized steel fire lookout towers under the "Aermotor Corporation" name

evidence.supports: Elk State Forest land obtained from lumber companies in the early 1900s
evidence.quote: The land was primarily acquired from lumber companies during the early 20th century.
The lumber era in the area of Elk State Forest lasted until 1915 when the last raft was floated down the Driftwood Branch.

evidence.supports: sparks from steam trains started fires that slowed regrowth after the lumber companies left
evidence.quote: Sparks cast off by passing steam trains ignited wildfires that slowed the growth of the thriving second growth forest of hardwoods that is now Elk State Forest.

sources.title: Fire Towers of Pennsylvania (story map item data)

notes_for_editor: Build year, builder and height come only from the storymap item data; no second source was found. The record spells the name Whitimore, and the storymap's own heading reads Whitimore Tower. Search results list it as Whittimore (a trail listing and a photo caption), but those pages returned 403 and 429 errors and were not read, so the spelling is unverified and should be checked before publication; the story does not yet mention the variant. Not in the NHLR Pennsylvania list. The FFLOS index has a Whittaker Tower Site, which is a different tower. The storymap also has a separate Sandy Ridge entry in Centre County, which is not this tower. Elk State Forest and Aermotor pages are used for context only. Access, staffing and climbing status are unknown; the story says so. Verification 2026-10-09: the storymap entry was re-read in context (1921, Aermotor Windmill Company, 47 ft); the Aermotor line now quotes the page's full phrase; the Elk sparks and acquisition sentences were reworded away from the source's wording.
